Summary Description: Dr. Patrick D. Manapat is a quantitative methodologist and psychologist whose research bridges psychometrics, replication science, and methodological theory within psychology. His work advances both instrument development and the evaluation of methodological practices through rigorous simulation studies and model-based diagnostics. Notable contributions include: (1) hierarchical extensions of the Dynamic Fit Index (DFI) to provide model-specific cutoffs for hierarchical/second-order factor models, (2) a taxonomy clarifying research vs. reporting practices and the SBO/RDF/QRP framework to reduce avoidable heterogeneity, (3) large-scale EFA replication studies (evaluating how decisions like factor number, rotation, and analysis type influence factor recovery), (4) robust psychometric evaluation of clinical instruments such as the Duke Misophonia Questionnaire (DMQ) using EFA/CFA, IRT/MIRT, and validity analyses, and (5) robustness investigations of unidimensional IRT models under nonnormal latent distributions. Across these strands, Manapat leverages R-based simulations, open-source tools, and collaborations to improve measurement validity, replication practices, and methodological transparency in psychology.

Representative Works.Title: Dynamic Fit Index Cutoffs for Hierarchical and Second-Order Factor Models
Representative Works.Note: Introduces hierarchical DFI with hier1HB (measurement misspecification) and hier2 (structural misspecification), including multi-level cutoffs and empirical demonstration with Reynolds & Keith (2017) data

Representative Works.Title: A Psychometric Analysis of the Duke Misophonia Questionnaire
Representative Works.Note: Comprehensive psychometric evaluation of DMQ using EFA, CFA, and Multidimensional IRT; supports a five-factor structure and validates convergent/divergent validity with related scales

Representative Works.Title: A Revised and Expanded Taxonomy for Understanding Heterogeneity in Research and Reporting Practices
Representative Works.Note: Proposes a two-arm taxonomy (research vs reporting practices) with SBO, RDF, and QRP distinctions; includes a simulated demonstration on assumption checking and Type I error

Representative Works.Title: Evaluating Avoidable Heterogeneity in Exploratory Factor Analysis Results
Representative Works.Note: Explores how garden-of-forking-path decisions in EFA (factor number, analysis path, rotation, scale version) affect replication-like outcomes; emphasizes reducing heterogeneity via robust decision rules

Representative Works.Title: Examining the Robustness of the Graded Response and 2-Parameter Logistic Models to Violations of Construct Normality
Representative Works.Note: Assesses GRM and 2PLM under nonnormal latent distributions using Fleishman transformations; provides practical sample-size guidelines and robustness patterns
